plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE (n=3) + power caveat + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a single bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12000 genes x 7 columns incl. gene symbol, 6 samples) from Salmon, liver tissue, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. With only 3 replicates per group the standard and only defensible path is DESeq2's Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, preceded by mandatory sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to catch an outlier or mislabeled sample before the model is fit, and followed by an edgeR quasi-likelihood run as a robustness cross-check (report the intersection as the high-confidence set). Because three replicates per group is a low-power regime, the plan explicitly reports the expected power/detectable effect-size limits and treats absence from the significant list as 'not detected', not as 'unchanged'. Differential expression feeds a preranked fgsea analysis (rank by the Wald statistic) against locally staged MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, with Reactome as a documented second-collection follow-up, since fewer than ~50 significant genes would make an over-representation test underpowered. A final report step consolidates DE tables, diagnostic plots, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the power caveat, and the enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata.

Minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size
DESeq2 design ~condition with explicit reference level
DESeq2 Wald test (primary) with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (secondary, robustness check)
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Integrated DE + power caveat + enrichment report
